This wouldn't go over nearly as easily in the European Union. We have much stronger consumer protection laws, and using compatible third-party ink cartridges is generally legal. A company forcing customers to buy only its own overpriced cartridges after an online update would likely face much greater scrutiny here.

Here in the Netherlands, we also have ink refill shops. If something like this happens, many people simply have their original OEM cartridges refilled instead of buying expensive new ones. Since they're still the original cartridges, this often bypasses these kinds of restrictions. It's cheaper, creates less waste, and is much more consumer-friendly.

We've seen something similar with Apple. The EU pushed back against practices that limited repairs to the manufacturer, leading to stronger right to repair rules that give consumers more choice and make it easier for independent repair shops to operate.
